title: FDR Fireside Chats
paragraphs: Frozen GRH container preserves 31 numbered Franklin D. Roosevelt radio addresses corresponding to the FDR Presidential Library list of 31 speeches identified as Fireside Chats. Institutional audiovisual guidance explicitly says the category is disputed: 28 definite, two questionable, and potentially as many as 33 under an extended definition.

GRH documents the program through Depression and New Deal chats (March 12, 1933 to June 24, 1938), European war, defense and U.S. entry (September 3, 1939 to December 9, 1941), and World War II home-front and war-progress chats (February 23, 1942 to January 6, 1945).
Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Franklin D. Roosevelt (speaker on 31 recordings).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include World War II, military progress and diplomacy, wartime home front, labor, prices and mobilization, New Deal recovery and federal programs, employment, relief, WPA and social security, economic conditions, prices and sacrifice, and national defense, emergency and military readiness.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Presidential radio communication and the Fireside Chat form, Great Depression and New Deal public explanation, European war and American defense mobilization, and World War II home front and military progress.
